rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) is controlled by checkpoints. Mitosis (PMAT) produces two genetically identical diploid cells for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction; cytokinesis differs between animal (cleavage furrow) and plant (cell plate) cells.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mitosis: 2n → 2 daughter cells of 2n
Meiosis: 2n → 4 gametes of n
Crossing over (Prophase I) + independent assortment (Metaphase I) → variation

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number (2n → 2n); meiosis halves it (2n → n).  ·  Crossing over and independent assortment occur in MEIOSIS only, not mitosis.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects labelled mitosis diagrams plus a full meiosis diagram with crossing over marked.  ·  The mitosis vs meiosis comparison table (6 points) is a very common question.

rows.label: Solved

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Spermatogenesis: 1 primary (2n) → 2 secondary (n) → 4 spermatids (n) → 4 sperm.  ·  Oogenesis: 1 primary (2n) → 1 secondary (n) + 1 polar body → 1 ovum (n) + 3 polar bodies.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED CELL DIVISION: the full cell cycle and every mitotic/meiotic phase.  ·  Interphase (90% of the cycle): G1 (growth, organelle duplication, protein synthesis), S (DNA replication — each chromosome now has 2 sister chromatids), G2 (preparation for mitosis, checkpoint).  ·  Checkpoints: G1/S (DNA damage, nutrients), G2/M (replication complete), M (spindle attachment) — failures cause cancer.
